title: Hybrid workload orchestration and CI perf gate for kernel-routing regressions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a new hybrid workload orchestration layer for the benchmark harness that composes synthetic seeds, production trace samples, and adversarial microbench slices to produce stable, reproducible golden baselines for kernel selection and prefill/decode scheduling. Add deterministic seeding, platform-aware sampling weights, and a CI perf gate which fails on regressions to critical latency and throughput metrics for kernel-routing paths. The goal is to detect regressions introduced by attention optimization changes, kernel selection heuristics, and prefill scheduling changes before they reach staging. This ticket covers design, implementation in the bench harness, integration with CI, and dashboards for triage.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can generate and run hybrid workloads that combine: 60% production-sampled traces, 30% synthetic long-context prefill sequences, 10% adversarial microbench slices, with deterministic seeds
Baseline golden run (runtime-1.20) produced and stored in artifact bucket with versioned metadata and hash
CI gate introduced that compares new runs to baseline and fails when p99 latency increases by >5% or aggregate tokens/sec drops >7% on kernel-routing paths
Bench runs annotated with kernel-selection decisions (kernel id, reason code), attention optimization flags, and prefill vs decode timing breakdowns
Triage dashboard with links to failing run artifacts, diffed kernel traces, and suggested rollback targets is available in Console
Documentation describing workload composition, sampling weights, seed generation, and how to interpret CI failures is merged
proposed_solution: Create a workload composer module in the bench harness that accepts a declarative profile (weights, seed, target length distribution, platform affinities). Implement deterministic sampler for production traces (using stable hashing + time bucketing) and a microbench generator for adversarial kernel/attention patterns (e.g., extreme sequence length, attention windowing). Extend the runner to capture kernel-routing telemetry and export an artifacts bundle (metrics, kernel traces, raw inputs). Add a CI step that runs the composer on a small but representative hardware fixture, compares metrics to the golden baseline with configurable thresholds, and annotates PRs with result summary and artifact links.
test_plan: Unit tests for workload composer: deterministic sampling across runs and platforms
Integration test: end-to-end run producing artifacts bundle and metrics on a CI fixture (mocked kernels for speed)
Experimental runs on staging fleet to validate stable baseline variance (run n=10 over 48h and compute CI width)
CI smoke gate: run on every PR touching runtime/kernel selection code with a reduced workload profile (fast but representative)
Canary rollout for CI thresholds: start with permissive thresholds for 2 weeks and tighten as baseline variance is quantified
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement composer and artifact export; land docs and baseline for runtime-1.20. Phase 2: wire fast CI smoke gate for PRs touching runtime and kernel routing (week 1). Phase 3: enable full CI gate on main branch for merge-blocking after 2 weeks of permissive monitoring. Phase 4: integrate gate with Console triage dashboards and automated rollback suggestions.
risks_and_mitigations: Flaky CI due to baseline variance: mitigate by measuring baseline variance across 10 runs and set thresholds to 3-sigma of noise
False positives from hardware heterogeneity: pin CI fixtures to a standardized hardware image and label workload profiles with platform-affinity
Large runtime for full runs: create a fast-repr profile for CI and keep full golden runs off CI to scheduled cadence
Telemetry volume and privacy: strip PII from traces and store only hashed identifiers and length distributions
